en: Even within me, who am consciousness—unparalleled, eternal, partless, indivisible, and devoid of all conceptual constructions—it is Māyā, expert in effecting the impossible, that brings about the distinction between the Lord of the Universe, the individual soul, and the world. || 1 ||

Alas, Māyā—capable of effecting the impossible and inseparable from the four-footed [animals] and so forth—immediately defiles even those who purify the Vedas and the Upaniṣads by means of examples such as wealth and the like. (2)
Having projected the non-dual, indivisible consciousness of bliss into that which is fashioned from space,
fire, and the other elements, Māyā— expert at effecting the impossible— causes one to wander incessantly in the ocean of worldly existence.

Illusion, which is expert at joining together what was not joined, makes manifest the egoism of the Vipras, Viḍas, and others— who are devoid of distinctions of quality, color, or caste— within this city of happiness, as well as the delusion regarding children, wives, and home.

Alas, Māyā—so adept at effecting the impossible—having created even the wise into the state of perceiving a distinction between Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva within that which is indivisible, causes them to wander excessively in their notions of difference between Hari and Hara. || 5 ||
Thus ends the Māyāpañcaka, composed by the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda, the illustrious wandering ascetic teacher (Paramahaṃsa-parivrājaka-ācārya).
